See also: Limonade and limonádé

Dutch

[edit]
Dutch Wikipedia has an article on:
limonade
Wikipedia nl

Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from French limonade.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /li.moːˈnaː.də/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Hyphenation: li‧mo‧na‧de
    • Rhymes: -aːdə

    Noun

    [edit]

    limonade f (plural limonades, diminutive limonadetje n)

    1. (Netherlands) sweetened drink (sweet drink based on processed fruit juice, may be based on cordial, may or may not be carbonated); a serving of sweetened drink
      Synonyms: limo, ranja
    2. (Belgium) soft drink, fizzy drink, soda (carbonated sweet drink based on processed fruit juice)
      Synonyms: fris, frisdrank, priklimonade
    3. (archaic) lemonade or any other lemon-based or lime-based sweetened drink
      Synonym: citroenlimonade

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • citroenlimonade
    • limo
    • limonadesiroop
    • priklimonade

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • → Aukan: ayomanali
    • → Caribbean Hindustani: nimnár
    • → Indonesian: limonade

    French

    [edit]
    French Wikipedia has an article on:
    limonade
    Wikipedia fr

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • limonnade (alternative spelling)

    Etymology

    [edit]

      From limon (“lemon”) +‎ -ade. Compare Italian limonata, Spanish limonada, Venetan łimonada.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /li.mɔ.nad/
      • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
      • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
      • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
      • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

      Noun

      [edit]

      limonade f (plural limonades)

      1. lemonade; a serving of lemonade
        Synonym: citronnade
        • 1640, Antoine Oudin, Recherches italiennes et françoises, ou Dictionnaire, Paris: Antoine de Sommaville, pages 219a, 465b, 781a, 863b:
          Citronata, limonade. Item, saulse faite avec du jus de citron.
          Citronata, lemonade. Likewise, a sauce made with lemon juice.
          Limonea, limonnade.
          Limonea, lemonade.
          Sorbetto, sorte de limonade. Item, petite gorgée.
          Sorbetto, kind of lemonade. Likewise, a small gulp.
          Tizerbetto, sorte de breuvage, comme la limonade.
          Tizerbetto, kind of beverage, like lemonade.
      2. a soda with a hint of lemon flavoring with sugar that is popular in France; a serving of this soda
      3. (dated) the general business of operating a bar or cafe
        • Il était sûrement dans la limonade depuis longtemps
          (please add an English translation of this quotation)

      Derived terms

      [edit]
      • limonaderie
      • limonadier

      Descendants

      [edit]
      • Mauritian Creole: limonad
      • Seychellois Creole: limonad
      • → Albanian: limonadë
      • → Dutch: limonade
        • → Aukan: ayomanali
        • → Caribbean Hindustani: nimnár
        • → Indonesian: limonade
      • → English: lemonade
        • → Japanese: レモネード (remonēdo)
        • → Korean: 레모네이드 (remoneideu)
        • → Unami: lèmënèt
        • → Welsh: lemonêd
      • → German: Limonade
        • → Hungarian: limonádé
        • → Slovene: limonȃda
      • → Russian: лимона́д (limonád)
        • → Armenian: լիմոնադ (limonad)
        • → Azerbaijani: limonad
        • → Crimean Tatar: limonad
        • → Kazakh: лимонад (limonad)

      Further reading

      [edit]
      • “limonade”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

      Indonesian

      [edit]
      Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
      limonade
      Wikipedia id

      Etymology

      [edit]

        Borrowed from Dutch limonade, from French limonade.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): /li.moˈna.də/, [li.moˈna.də]
        • Rhymes: -də
        • Hyphenation: li‧mo‧na‧dê

        Noun

        [edit]

        limonadê (plural limonade-limonade)

        1. lemonade:
          1. a flavoured beverage consisting of water, lemon, and sweetener, sometimes ice, served mainly as a refreshment
          2. a clear, usually carbonated, beverage made from lemon or artificial lemon flavouring, water, and sugar

        Alternative forms

        [edit]
        • limun

        Further reading

        [edit]
        • “limonade”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016
